Builds an `Assume` from a lang-item `TransmuteOpts` const by evaluating the const, defaulting all assumptions to `true` if evaluation reported an error, asserting the const has the expected ADT, and decoding the `alignment`, `lifetimes`, `safety`, and `validity` fields from its `ValTree`. It does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/consts.rs::: Returns the cached type of the interned constant from `self.0.ty`. It does not call other listed methods.
Returns the cached `ConstKind` of the interned constant from `self.0.kind`. It does not call other listed methods.

Lowers an HIR anonymous const into `ty::Const` by extracting its body and type, trying to eagerly convert literal/parameter forms, and otherwise producing an unevaluated const with identity args. It explicitly calls `hir_node_by_def_id`, `def_span`, `to_def_id`, `hir`, `body`, `type_of`, `no_bound_vars`, `expect`, `Const::try_from_lit_or_param`, `Const::new_unevaluated`, and `identity_for_item`.

Attempts to convert an expression into a constant immediately. It unwraps trivial blocks, recognizes literal and negated-literal expressions and lowers them through `lit_to_const`, and recognizes resolved const-parameter paths to construct a `Param` const via `mk_const`. Returns `Some(Const)` for those supported cases and `None` otherwise.
Extracts the underlying `ValTree` from a constant known to have `ConstKind::Value`, panicking otherwise. It inspects the constant kind via `kind`.

Constructs a value constant from raw integer bits by computing the target layout size and wrapping the bits as a scalar `ValTree`. It explicitly calls `layout_of`, `unwrap_or_else`, `Const::new_value`, `from_scalar_int`, `try_from_uint`, and `unwrap`.
Constructs the canonical zero-sized value constant for the given type. It explicitly calls `Const::new_value` and `zst`.
Constructs a boolean constant by forwarding to the raw-bits constructor with the builtin `bool` type. It explicitly calls `Const::from_bits`, `empty`, and `and`.
Constructs a target-`usize` constant by forwarding to the raw-bits constructor with the builtin `usize` type. It explicitly calls `Const::from_bits`, `empty`, and `and`.

Evaluates the constant to raw bits by first obtaining a scalar integer and then interpreting it using the constant type's layout size. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar_int` and `self.ty()` from this methods list, while also querying `tcx.layout_of(...)` to determine the bit width.
Evaluates the constant to a boolean by first obtaining a scalar integer and then attempting a boolean conversion. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar_int`.
Evaluates the constant to a target-sized `usize` value if possible. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar_int` and then converts the result with `try_to_target_usize`.

Evaluates a constant to a `ValTree` when possible: unevaluated consts are prepared and resolved through type-checking const-eval, value consts are returned directly, error consts propagate their error, and param/infer/bound/placeholder/expr consts are rejected as too generic. It explicitly calls `has_escaping_bound_vars`, `Const::kind`, `prepare_for_eval`, `const_eval_resolve_for_typeck`, `dcx`, `span_delayed_bug`, and `into`.
Returns the evaluated raw bits of the constant, panicking with `bug!` if bit evaluation fails. It explicitly calls `try_eval_bits`, and uses `self.ty()` when formatting the failure message.
Returns the evaluated target-sized `usize` value of the constant, panicking with `bug!` if evaluation fails. It explicitly calls `try_eval_target_usize`.
Checks whether this constant is an inference constant. It inspects the constant kind via `kind` and matches `ConstKind::Infer`.

Retrieves the default value for a local const generic parameter from HIR and wraps it in an `EarlyBinder`. It explicitly calls `Const::from_anon_const` to lower the anonymous constant after locating the default const definition.

Formats a `Const` in the legacy debug style `Const { ty: ..., kind: ... }`. This method explicitly calls `ty` and `kind` on `self` to obtain the constant’s type and kind for printing, and then delegates formatting to `write!`/`fmt` machinery.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Dispatches confirmation based on the selected `SelectionCandidate`, builds the corresponding `ImplSource`, and then fixes returned nested obligation depths before producing the final `Selection`. It explicitly calls `confirm_builtin_candidate`, `confirm_transmutability_candidate`, `confirm_param_candidate`, `confirm_impl_candidate`, `confirm_auto_impl_candidate`, `confirm_projection_candidate`, `confirm_object_candidate`, `confirm_closure_candidate`, `confirm_async_closure_candidate`, `confirm_coroutine_candidate`, `confirm_future_candidate`, `confirm_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_async_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_fn_pointer_candidate`, `confirm_trait_alias_candidate`, `confirm_builtin_unsize_candidate`, and `confirm_trait_upcasting_unsize_candidate`.

Confirms a projection-derived candidate by recovering the indexed item-bound trait clause from the self type, instantiating and normalizing it, equating it with the obligation trait ref, and adding any extra predicates from projection aliases. It explicitly calls `normalize_with_depth_to` to normalize both the selected trait clause and any alias predicates.

Replays where-clause matching for a parameter candidate and returns the resulting nested obligations, treating any mismatch after prior evaluation as an internal bug. It explicitly calls `match_where_clause_trait_ref`.

Confirms builtin trait candidates by computing the builtin-specific conditions and converting any required component types into nested obligations; candidates without nested requirements return no obligations. It explicitly calls `sized_conditions`, `copy_clone_conditions`, `fused_iterator_conditions`, and `collect_predicates_for_types`.

Confirms a transmutability candidate by evaluating the transmute relation, translating the resulting condition tree into nested trait, lifetime, and freeze obligations, and returning those obligations or an error. It explicitly calls the local helpers `flatten_answer_tree` and `reference_obligations`.
Confirms an auto-trait candidate by resolving the self type, extracting its constituent types, and deriving the auto-trait vtable obligations from them. It explicitly calls `vtable_auto_impl`.

Constructs the nested obligations for an auto-trait impl by combining obligations implied by the trait definition itself with obligations collected from the constituent nested types. It explicitly calls `impl_or_trait_obligations` and `collect_predicates_for_types`.
Confirms a user-defined impl candidate by rematching the impl to obtain concrete args and then building the impl source data from that match. It explicitly calls `rematch_impl` and `vtable_impl`.

Builds `ImplSourceUserDefinedData` for a concrete impl by collecting the impl or trait predicates induced by the chosen args and then extending them with normalization obligations carried in the matched args. It explicitly calls `impl_or_trait_obligations`.

Confirms a trait-object candidate by selecting the indexed supertrait from the object's principal trait, normalizing and equating it with the obligation, then adding obligations for explicit supertraits and associated-type bounds needed by the object. It explicitly calls `normalize_with_depth_to`.

Confirms a function-pointer candidate by building the corresponding closure-trait reference from the function signature, equating it with the obligation, and adding the `Output: Sized` obligation required by `FnOnce`. It explicitly calls `equate_trait_refs` and `normalize_with_depth_to`.
Confirms a trait-alias candidate by expanding the alias into the obligations implied by the aliased trait definition. It explicitly calls `impl_or_trait_obligations`.
Confirms a future candidate by deriving the `Future` trait reference from the coroutine signature and equating it with the obligation. It explicitly calls `equate_trait_refs`.

Confirms a closure candidate by constructing the expected closure trait reference for either a normal closure or coroutine closure and then unifying it with the obligation. It explicitly calls `equate_trait_refs`.

Normalizes the obligation trait reference together with the expected self-type trait reference, then checks that the obligation is a supertrait-compatible match and returns the combined nested obligations. It explicitly calls `normalize_with_depth` to normalize both trait refs under `ensure_sufficient_stack`, then uses `at(...).sup(...)` to relate the normalized obligation trait ref to the expected trait ref, extends the returned obligations with the normalization obligations, and converts relation failures into `SelectionError::OutputTypeParameterMismatch`.

Confirms a trait-upcasting unsize candidate by extracting the source and target dyn principals, selecting the indexed supertrait principal from the source, and matching that upcast against the target object to produce builtin trait-upcasting obligations. It explicitly calls `match_upcast_principal`.

Confirms builtin unsizing by analyzing the resolved source and target types and producing the appropriate `ImplSource` plus nested obligations for dyn upcasts, pointer/array unsizing, and related builtin coercions. It does not explicitly call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Confirms a `~const Destruct` candidate by first short-circuiting in the current non-const path, otherwise checking any explicit const-drop impl and then deriving recursive obligations from the structure of the self type. When an `impl_def_id` is present, it explicitly calls `rematch_impl` to recover impl arguments and `vtable_impl` under `ensure_sufficient_stack` to validate the impl and collect its nested obligations; afterward it inspects the resolved self type, expands ADT fields into a work stack, and walks constituent types to accumulate additional destruct-related obligations.

Confirms a generator trait candidate by resolving the obligation self type to a concrete `ty::Generator`, extracting its signature, constructing the expected generator trait reference for the obligation, and unifying it against the obligation to produce nested predicate obligations and `ImplSourceGeneratorData`. Calls `confirm_poly_trait_refs` to perform the trait-ref confirmation; it also uses `shallow_resolve` and `self_ty`/`skip_binder` to inspect the generator self type, and `generator_trait_ref_and_outputs` to build the expected trait ref.

Main entry point for trait-candidate collection. It resolves the obligation, fast-rejects ambiguous `Self` type variables, then dispatches to specialized assemblers based on polarity and the target trait/lang item. For negative predicates it calls `assemble_candidates_for_trait_alias`, `assemble_candidates_from_impls`, and `assemble_candidates_from_caller_bounds`. For positive predicates it always calls `assemble_candidates_for_trait_alias`, and then conditionally calls `assemble_candidates_from_impls`, `assemble_builtin_bound_candidates`, `assemble_candidates_for_unsizing`, `assemble_const_destruct_candidates`, `assemble_candidates_for_transmutability`, `assemble_candidate_for_tuple`, `assemble_candidates_for_fn_ptr_trait`, `assemble_coroutine_candidates`, `assemble_future_candidates`, `assemble_iterator_candidates`, `assemble_fused_iterator_candidates`, `assemble_async_iterator_candidates`, `assemble_async_fn_kind_helper_candidates`, `assemble_closure_candidates`, `assemble_async_closure_candidates`, `assemble_fn_pointer_candidates`, `assemble_candidates_from_object_ty`, `assemble_candidates_from_projected_tys`, `assemble_candidates_from_caller_bounds`, and `assemble_candidates_from_auto_impls` to populate the final `SelectionCandidateSet`.

Adds projection-based candidates when the obligation `Self` type is a projection or opaque alias. It instantiates placeholders, enumerates item bounds with `for_each_item_bound`, uses `match_normalize_trait_ref` to test each trait bound against the obligation, deduplicates normalized matches, pushes `ProjectionCandidate`s for matching bounds, and marks ambiguity when matching or normalization cannot conclusively enumerate distinct bounds.

Collects `ParamCandidate`s from the obligation’s caller-provided bounds. It skips error-containing predicates, filters caller bounds to the same trait and polarity, uses deep-reject unification plus `where_clause_may_apply` to keep only potentially applicable bounds, and pushes a parameter candidate for each surviving bound. This method calls `where_clause_may_apply`.
Adds a `FutureCandidate` when the obligation `Self` type is a coroutine lowered from an async construct, identified via `coroutine_is_async`.

Builds `ClosureCandidate`s for `Fn`/`FnMut`/`FnOnce` obligations on closures and coroutine-closures. It determines the requested function-trait kind, inspects closure kind information, accepts compatible ordinary closures, and applies the coroutine-closure-specific rules for `FnOnce`, self-borrows, and unconstrained upvars, marking ambiguity when the closure kind is not yet known.

Builds `FnPointerCandidate`s for `Fn`-family traits on callable function pointers and function items. It first checks that the target trait is a function trait, then accepts compatible `fn` pointers and function definitions, rejects `#[target_feature]` function items, and marks type-variable self types as ambiguous.

Collects user-written impl candidates for the obligation. It skips obligations containing error types, quick-rejects impls whose trait arguments cannot unify, ignores default impls, filters impls through `reject_fn_ptr_impls`, then probes `match_impl` and pushes an `ImplCandidate` for each impl that matches. This method calls `reject_fn_ptr_impls` and `match_impl`.

Special-case filter used during impl assembly to reject impls whose self type is a generic parameter constrained by the `FnPtr` lang-item trait when the obligation self type is definitely not a function pointer. It scans the impl predicates for the `FnPtr` bound and, for potentially compatible abstract self types, builds and evaluates the corresponding root obligation with `evaluate_root_obligation`; otherwise it returns an immediate accept/reject answer based on the concrete self-type kind.

Adds builtin auto-trait candidates when the target trait is auto and the self type is suitable for structural auto-impl reasoning. It avoids object/foreign/abstract types, marks inference variables as ambiguous, handles coroutine movability as a special builtin case, suppresses duplicate projection-derived auto candidates in some opaque-type modes, and pushes builtin candidates for concrete types whose components can be checked structurally.

Builds object-based candidates for traits that may be implemented via trait objects. Inside a probe, it resolves the obligation, examines dynamic self types, immediately adds a `BuiltinObjectCandidate` when the object explicitly carries the auto trait, otherwise inspects the principal trait and its supertraits, uses `match_normalize_trait_ref` to find matching upcasts, and records corresponding `ObjectCandidate`s; unresolved type variables are marked ambiguous. This method calls `match_normalize_trait_ref`.

Checks whether unsizing should use the legacy deref-output trait-object migration path. It rejects coherence mode and enabled trait-upcasting, tests whether `<ty as Deref>` may hold, then calls `normalize_projection_ty` to compute `Deref::Target` and returns its principal existential trait if that target normalizes to a trait object. This method calls `normalize_projection_ty`.

Builds candidates for `Unsize` obligations. It first requires a concrete source type without bound regions, then handles trait-object upcasting, auto-trait dropping, principal-trait upcasts, deref-output migration, array-to-slice unsizing, and structural unsizing for structs and tuples. During trait-object handling it calls `need_migrate_deref_output_trait_object`, and for principal upcasts it probes `match_upcast_principal` to push `TraitUpcastingUnsizeCandidate`s when an upcast is valid.

Adds a `TransmutabilityCandidate` only when the predicate has no non-region generic parameters and no non-region inference variables; otherwise it either returns with no candidate or marks the result ambiguous.
Adds a `TraitAliasCandidate` when the obligation’s trait `def_id` refers to a trait alias.

Converts builtin-impl condition results into candidate-set state: it pushes a `BuiltinCandidate` when the conditions are satisfied, setting `has_nested` from the nested obligations, does nothing for `None`, and marks the set ambiguous for `Ambiguous`.
Unconditionally adds a builtin candidate for the const-destruct trait with no nested obligations.
Adds a builtin candidate when the resolved self type is a tuple, marks unresolved type-variable self types as ambiguous, and otherwise produces no candidate for non-tuple types.

Builds a builtin candidate for pointer-like types by erasing bound regions from the obligation self type and param-env, marking the candidate set ambiguous if the resulting key still has non-region inference variables, and otherwise querying layout to see whether the type is pointer-like before pushing a builtin candidate. Calls `tcx`, `erase_late_bound_regions`, `self_ty`, `erase_regions`, `and`, `has_non_region_infer`, `layout_of`, `is_pointer_like`, and `push`.

Adds a builtin candidate for the `FnPtr` trait when the resolved self type is a function pointer. Concrete non-function-pointer types produce no candidate, while unconstrained type variables and fresh type variables mark the result ambiguous.

Collects `GeneratorCandidate` for `Generator` trait obligations whose `self` type is a non-async generator. It calls `self_ty` and `skip_binder` to inspect the obligation self type, then calls `kind` to match on that type. For `ty::Generator`, it calls `tcx` and `generator_is_async` to exclude async generators before pushing a `GeneratorCandidate`; for `ty::Infer(TyVar(_))`, it marks the candidate set as ambiguous instead of adding a candidate.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_const_eval/src/const_eval: Builds a `ValTree::Branch` for tuple/struct/enum fields by optionally downcasting to an enum variant, recursively converting each projected field with `const_to_valtree_inner`, and prepending the variant index for enums.
Builds a `ValTree::Branch` for slice-like data by iterating indices of the place and recursively converting each element with `const_to_valtree_inner`.

Recursively converts an interpreter place into a type-level `ValTree`, handling scalars directly, dereferencing references and then calling `const_to_valtree_inner` again, using `slice_branches` for strings/slices/arrays, and using `branches` for tuples and ADTs; rejects unsupported or equality-unsound kinds and enforces the valtree node limit.

Converts a `ValTree` back into `mir::ConstValue`: trivial scalar kinds become immediate scalars, references are rebuilt by creating an eval context and calling `valtree_to_ref`, and aggregate values either recurse into `valtree_to_const_value` for scalar tuple/struct fast paths or allocate/rebuild storage via `create_valtree_place` and `valtree_into_mplace` before turning the result into a const.

Recursively writes a `ValTree` into an interpreter memory place: scalars are written directly, references are rebuilt via `valtree_to_ref`, and aggregates/enums descend into projected fields or elements and call `valtree_into_mplace` recursively; it also uses `dump_place` for tracing and writes enum discriminants after filling variant fields.
Small tracing helper that dumps the contents of an interpreter place for debugging; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Allocates a stack-backed interpreter memory place for `ty` by computing its layout with `tcx.layout_of(...)` and then calling `ecx.allocate(...)` with that layout.

Finds the unsized tail field type and element count for a valtree-backed DST. It calls `tcx.struct_tail_with_normalize(...)` to walk to the structural tail while updating `last_valtree`, then uses `unwrap_branch()` on the valtree to descend and finally reads the last branch length as the unsized field length.

Creates an interpreter place for the pointee described by `ty` and `valtree`. For unsized types, it calls `get_info_on_unsized_field(...)` to recover the DST element type and length, computes the total allocation size from layouts, allocates raw memory with `ecx.allocate_ptr(...)`, and builds an `MPlaceTy` with metadata via `MPlaceTy::from_aligned_ptr_with_meta(...)`. For sized types, it directly calls `create_mplace_from_layout(...)`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/mir/interpret/: Builds identity generic arguments for a non-generic constant item, wraps them in an `Instance` and `GlobalId`, normalizes the item's parameter environment with reveal-all, and then calls `const_eval_global_id` to perform const-value evaluation.

Resolves an `mir::UnevaluatedConst` under the given parameter environment after rejecting inference-containing args; on successful `ty::Instance::resolve`, it creates a `GlobalId` and calls `const_eval_global_id`, otherwise returning `TooGeneric` or a reported resolution error.

Resolves a `ty::UnevaluatedConst` for type checking after rejecting inference-containing args; on successful `ty::Instance::resolve`, it creates a `GlobalId` and calls `const_eval_global_id_for_typeck`, then inspects successful results to emit the `CONST_EVALUATABLE_UNCHECKED` lint for unsupported polymorphic generic const expressions.
Thin wrapper that packages an already-resolved `Instance` into a `GlobalId` and calls `const_eval_global_id`.

Performs the shared const-value query setup by reveal-all normalizing the parameter environment, combining it with the `GlobalId`, erasing regions for caching, and then calling `eval_to_const_value_raw` directly or via `at(span)` so query errors can be remapped to the provided span.

Performs the shared type-checking const-evaluation setup by reveal-all normalizing the parameter environment, combining it with the `GlobalId`, erasing regions for caching, and then calling `eval_to_valtree` directly or via `at(span)` so query errors can be remapped to the provided span.

Evaluates the initializer of a static item after asserting the `DefId` is static. It builds a monomorphic `Instance` with `mono`, wraps it in a `GlobalId`, and then calls `eval_to_allocation` with `ParamEnv::reveal_all()` to obtain the final memory allocation.

Evaluates a static item's initializer into a `ConstAllocation`. It asserts the given `DefId` is static by calling `is_static`, constructs a monomorphic `Instance` with `ty::Instance::mono`, builds a `GlobalId`, and then delegates the actual allocation evaluation to `eval_to_allocation` using `ty::ParamEnv::reveal_all()`.

Evaluates a `GlobalId` into a `ConstAllocation` for the given parameter environment. It calls `eval_to_allocation_raw` on `param_env.and(gid)` to obtain the raw allocation result, then resolves the final memory allocation by calling `global_alloc(...).unwrap_memory()`.

Ensures raw const evaluation for a non-generic constant item by building identity generic arguments, creating an `Instance` and `GlobalId`, normalizing the item's parameter environment with reveal-all, erasing regions, and calling `eval_to_const_value_raw`.

Forces evaluation of a static initializer query without returning the allocation. It asserts the `DefId` is static by calling `self.tcx.is_static`, creates a monomorphic `Instance` with `ty::Instance::mono`, builds a `GlobalId`, uses `ty::ParamEnv::reveal_all()`, and then directly triggers the underlying query by calling `eval_to_allocation_raw` on `param_env.and(gid)`.

Wraps infallible MIR constant destructuring by combining `param_env` and `constant` into a query input, calling `try_destructure_mir_constant`, and then `unwrap`ping the result to return `mir::DestructuredConstant`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Main entry point for const-evaluatability checking. It expands abstract consts with `expand_abstract_consts`, inspects the result via `kind`, and immediately accepts trivial const kinds or rejects `Infer`. When `generic_const_exprs` is enabled, it re-expands the const, checks whether an unevaluated const is an anon const via `def_kind`, and for non-anon consts calls `satisfied_from_param_env`; if that fails, it uses `has_non_region_infer` and `has_non_region_param` to classify the failure. As a fallback for unevaluated consts, it calls `const_eval_resolve` to actually evaluate the const and maps evaluation errors into `NotConstEvaluatable`, while unsupported `ConstKind::Expr` triggers compiler bugs/diagnostics.

Checks whether a const can be justified by `ConstEvaluatable` predicates in the parameter environment. It iterates over `caller_bounds`, filters `ConstEvaluatable` clauses through `kind` and `skip_binder`, expands each candidate with `expand_abstract_consts`, and visits the candidate const tree with `visit_with`. During that traversal it relies on `visit_const` to test whether the queried const matches a predicate or one of its abstract-const subexpressions, and accepts only a unique successful match.

Visitor callback that tests one const candidate from a `ConstEvaluatable` predicate subtree against the queried const. It calls `probe` to try the match without side effects, creates an `ObligationCtxt` with `new`, uses `eq` on both const types and values, and requires `select_all_or_error` to be empty before recording a match; it also tracks whether the match is unique. If the candidate’s `kind` is `Expr`, it recursively calls `visit_with`, which leads back to `visit_const` for nested const subexpressions.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Computes the semantic type of a local anonymous constant by inspecting its HIR parent and choosing the expected type from context. It directly calls `type_of` when the anon const is the default value of a const generic parameter, and otherwise derives types for array lengths/repeat counts, reserved `typeof(...)`, inline asm operands, enum discriminants, and other const-generic positions, producing diagnostics or error types for unexpected contexts.

Walks a pattern tree to find the resolved path whose generic argument list contains the target argument HIR id. It uses a local path-membership check while visiting struct, tuple-struct, and path patterns, and returns the first matching path if found.

Computes `type_of` for local HIR items and returns the result wrapped in an early binder. It directly calls `infer_placeholder_type` for constants whose type was written as `_`, `check_feature_inherent_assoc_ty` when handling inherent associated types, and `type_alias_is_lazy` when deciding how to treat type aliases; it also handles RPITIT cases up front by querying return-position impl-trait information and building the appropriate function, opaque, lowered, or error type for each item kind.

Infers a concrete type for an item declared with a placeholder `_` type by reading the body’s typeck result and improving diagnostics with a concrete suggestion when possible. It calls `bad_placeholder` when no stashed parser diagnostic can be reused, and otherwise emits or updates diagnostics before returning either the inferred type or an error type.

Checks whether the `inherent_associated_types` feature is enabled and emits the corresponding feature-gate error when it is not. This helper performs only the feature validation and diagnostic emission.

Finds the hidden type for a type-alias `impl Trait` by walking the defining scope, collecting candidate opaque-type constraints from items, impl items, trait items, and closures, and reconciling them into one result. It drives `ConstraintLocator::check` to inspect each potential defining use, relies on the visitor methods `nested_visit_map`, `visit_expr`, `visit_item`, `visit_impl_item`, and `visit_trait_item` to traverse HIR, and falls back to diagnostics/error types when no consistent constraint is found.

Checks whether a specific local item contributes a constraint for the target opaque type. It calls `has_typeck_results` to skip irrelevant items, `typeck` to read typeck-discovered opaque types, `ty_error` to record tainted error cases, `mir_borrowck` to obtain the concrete hidden type with regions, and `report_mismatch` when a newly found concrete type conflicts with the previously recorded one.
Supplies the HIR map used by the visitor while traversing the defining scope. It calls `hir`.

Visits expressions during opaque-type constraint search, checking closure bodies as potential defining uses before continuing traversal. It calls `check` for `Closure` expressions and then `walk_expr`.
Visits items in the reveal scope, skipping the opaque type item itself, and treats other items as possible sources of hidden-type constraints. It calls `check` on eligible items and then `walk_item`.
Visits impl items in the reveal scope, excluding the opaque type itself, and checks each remaining impl item for hidden-type constraints. It calls `check` and then `walk_impl_item`.
Visits trait items and checks each one for constraints on the target opaque type before recursing into it. It calls `check` and then `walk_trait_item`.

Validates the hidden type for a return-position `impl Trait` by taking the owner’s inferred hidden type and then walking the owner body/scope to ensure all nested defining uses agree with it. It drives `ConstraintChecker::check` to compare borrowck-derived opaque types, uses the visitor methods `nested_visit_map`, `visit_expr`, `visit_item`, `visit_impl_item`, and `visit_trait_item` for traversal, and falls back to `typeck`, `ty_error`, and `mk_diverging_default` when the owner has no usable hidden type.

Checks one local definition for borrowck-produced constraints on the target RPIT opaque type and reports any disagreement with the already chosen hidden type. It calls `mir_borrowck` to inspect concrete opaque types and `report_mismatch` when a non-error mismatch is found.
Supplies the HIR map for the RPIT constraint-checking visitor. It calls `hir`.
Visits expressions while validating RPIT constraints, checking closure bodies as additional defining uses before recursing. It calls `check` for `Closure` expressions and then `walk_expr`.
Visits items in the RPIT reveal scope, skipping the opaque type itself, and validates each remaining item as a potential source of constraints. It calls `check` and then `walk_item`.
Visits impl items during RPIT validation, excluding the opaque type itself, and checks each eligible impl item for matching constraints. It calls `check` and then `walk_impl_item`.
Visits trait items during RPIT validation and checks each one for consistency with the chosen hidden type before recursing. It calls `check` and then `walk_trait_item`.

Builds the canonical `ty::Generics` for a local definition by analyzing its HIR kind and parent context, with special handling for RPITITs, delegation, nested items, anon consts, const defaults, const blocks, closures, and opaque types. It calls `has_late_bound_regions` to detect whether the resulting generics should record late-bound regions.

Helper for function-like signatures that first checks generic lifetime parameters for `tcx.is_late_bound`, then traverses the function declaration with `LateBoundRegionsDetector` and returns any recorded span. It calls `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_ty@445-457`, `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_poly_trait_ref@459-466`, and `impl<'tcx> Visitor<'tcx> for LateBoundRegionsDetector<'tcx>::visit_lifetime@468-486` indirectly via `visitor.visit_fn_decl(decl)`.
